intro: Moving the object to the front, the pronoun that must then repeat it, things that happen by themselves, and le for lo.
p.duplicar.consejo: In grammar, to «duplicar» the object is to repeat it with a pronoun: «a Juan lo vi».
p.énfasis.consejo: It has an accent: EN-fa-sis. It is masculine: «el énfasis». It does not change in the plural.
p.destacar.consejo: Moving the object forward highlights it: «el libro lo compré ayer». The c sounds k.
p.leísmo.glosa: use of le instead of lo
p.leísmo.consejo: The RAE accepts it only for a male person: «le vi». Not for things: «lo compré».
p.romperse.consejo: With «se» there is nobody to blame: «se rompió el vaso». With «me»: «se me rompió».
p.estropearse.consejo: A machine or a car breaks down: «se me estropeó el paraguas».
p.apagarse.glosa: to go out, to switch off
p.apagarse.consejo: A light «se apaga» by itself. If you do it, «apago la luz». The g is hard: a-pa-GAR-se.
p.caerse.consejo: It is irregular: «se me cayó». It has two vowels together: ka-ER-se.
p.perderse.consejo: With «se me» it is something that vanishes with nobody to blame: «se me perdieron las llaves».
p.mancharse.consejo: Something gets stained by itself or by accident: «se me manchó la camisa». The ch sounds as in «chocolate».
p.sin querer.consejo: It is used to say it was not intended: «lo rompí sin querer».
p.a propósito.consejo: It is the opposite of «sin querer»: «lo hice a propósito». It also serves to change the subject.
b1.texto:
Spanish word order is flexible, but there is a price. If you put the object before the verb, you must repeat it with a pronoun.

- Vi **a Juan** ayer. → **A Juan lo** vi ayer.
- Compré **las entradas** por internet. → **Las entradas las** compré por internet.
- Ya sé **eso**. → **Eso** ya **lo** sé.
- Di el libro **a tu hermana**. → **A tu hermana le** di el libro.

Why do it? To start from what you are already talking about: **¿Y el coche? El coche lo** tiene mi hermano.

**Indirect objects** are different: the pronoun usually appears even when nothing has moved. **Le** di el libro **a tu hermana** is more natural than «di el libro a tu hermana».

**Stressed pronouns never go alone.** **A mí me** gusta. **A ella la** llamaron. **A nosotros** no **nos** dijeron nada. You cannot say «a ella llamaron».

**New information goes last.** That is why the subject often follows the verb: **Ha llegado una carta. Me lo dijo tu madre. Llamó Pedro.**
b2.f1.texto: I left the tickets on the table.
b2.f3.texto: You didn't say anything to me.
b2.f4.texto: And they are not on the table.
b2.f5.texto: Then I must have dropped them in the car.
b2.f6.texto: That I really hadn't thought of.
b2.f7.texto: You go to the car: my umbrella has broken.
b2.f9.texto: I promised your brother that we wouldn't be late.
b4.texto:
**Something happens with nobody to blame.** With **se**, an action has no author: **la puerta se abrió**; **el vaso se rompió**; **la luz se apagó**; **el coche se estropeó**.

Add a second pronoun and you say whom it happened to, still without blame: **se me rompió** el vaso; **se te ha caído** un guante; **se nos estropeó** el coche; **se le perdieron** las llaves.

Compare: **Rompí** el vaso (I did it) and **Se me rompió** el vaso (it happened to me). **Lo hice a propósito** against **fue sin querer**.

The verb agrees with the thing: se me **perdió** la llave; se me **perdieron** las llaves.

**Le vi or lo vi?** The direct object pronouns are **lo** and **la**. In much of Spain, however, people say **le** for a man: **A Juan le vi ayer**. This is called **leísmo**, and for a single male person the Academy accepts it. It is not accepted for things (el libro **lo** compré, never «le compré»). If in doubt, use **lo** and **la**: they are always correct.
b4.e0.texto: I broke the glass by accident.
b5.f0.texto: When evening falls, the light of the lamp goes out without a sound.
b5.f1.texto: The house is left in a blue half-light, full of long shadows.
b5.f2.texto: A cup falls from Rosa's hands.
b5.f3.texto: The porcelain breaks, by accident, into a thousand shining pieces.
b5.f4.texto: A smell of hot tea rises slowly to the ceiling.
b5.f5.texto: Rosa bends down and gathers the pieces with careful fingers.
b5.f6.texto: The sleeve of her blue dress gets a little stained.
b5.f7.texto: She did none of this on purpose.
b5.f8.texto: On the other side of the window, the rain begins to fall gently.
b5.f9.texto: In the silence, the sound of Rosa's footsteps along the hallway fades away.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the fronted object is repeated and agrees with «las llaves».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Les» is for an indirect object; «las llaves» is a direct object.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Lo» is masculine singular and «las llaves» is feminine plural.
b6.pregunta: Repeat the fronted object with a pronoun.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «a ella» needs the short pronoun «la».
b7.o1.refuerzo: The pronoun «la» that repeats «ella» is missing.
b8.frase: A mí no me dijiste nada
b8.traduccion: You didn't say anything to me
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «se me cayó» says it happened to the speaker.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Lo» is a direct object pronoun; here «me» goes.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Mi» is possessive; here you need the pronoun «me».
b9.pregunta: It happened to the speaker: choose the pronoun.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «le» is not accepted for things, only «lo».
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is accepted in Spain for a male person.
b11.o2.refuerzo: It is the always correct form.
b11.pregunta: Which sentence is not accepted in standard Spanish?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it repeats «eso» as the direct object.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Le» is for an indirect object, for persons.
b12.pregunta: Repeat «eso» with the pronoun for things.
p.habrán.consejo: Future of «haber», to have. The h is silent: a-BRAN.
p.pensado.consejo: Participle of «pensar», to think. Stress on SA.
p.prometí.consejo: Past tense of «prometer», to promise. The accent marks the stress on TI.
p.porcelana.consejo: Feminine, «la porcelana». The c before e is th. Stress on LA.
p.recoge.consejo: From «recoger», to pick up. The g before e is h: rre-KO-he.
p.cuidadosos.consejo: Plural of «cuidadoso», careful. Stress on DO.
p.manga.consejo: Feminine, «la manga». The g before a is hard. Stress on MAN.
p.llamaron.consejo: Past tense of «llamar», to call. The ll sounds like y.
p.cayó.consejo: Past tense of «caer», to fall. The accent marks the stress on YO.
p.sabía.consejo: Imperfect of «saber», to know. The accent separates the vowels: sa-BI-a.
p.llegaríamos.consejo: Conditional of «llegar», to arrive. The ll sounds like y.
